correctness.rationale: The F2-linear square map plus Fitting decomposition reduces any idempotent equation to invertible Bσx=x; explicit normal basis gives all 2^r geometric points with Frobenius B^{-1}. Pairwise-coprime quadratic leading monomials and identity Jacobian prove exact point count and étaleness. Möbius inversion gives closed-point counts; eigenvalue orders give δ≤2^n−1 and iff primitive irreducible equality; all extremal nonzero points form one orbit. Bounded full finite-field tests of original algebra identities succeeded for 2,208 configurations (including primitive cubic through F128), not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: It exactly measures and sharply optimizes the minimal extension degree needed to produce a nonzero idempotent of a perfect binary evolution algebra, a natural structure-theoretic obstruction across every dimension. The bound is attained at exponentially large degree and all attaining matrices are classified. The exact single closed point of maximal degree and zeta profile provide an arithmetic signature beyond finite base-field existence; finite graph formulas do not capture primitive companion extremizers. The result has a motivated object/invariant and is not an arbitrary parameter slice.
